title: Review 1: Yarn counts and yarn mixtures

quizzes.title: Key terms across the lectures
quizzes.intro: The language of yarn numbering, from Ne and tex to resultant counts.

questions.q: Which pair are both indirect count systems (a higher number means a finer yarn)?
questions.explain: Ne and Nm measure length per unit weight. Tex, dtex and denier measure weight per unit length.

questions.q: English cotton count (Ne) is the number of
questions.explain: Ne 20 means twenty hanks of 840 yards weigh one pound.

questions.q: Denier is the weight in grams of
questions.explain: Denier = grams per 9,000 metres; tex = grams per 1,000 metres, so denier = 9 × tex.

questions.q: The count of two or more yarns taken together as one is called the
questions.explain: When yarns run together or are twisted, their combined fineness is the resultant count.

questions.q: In a direct system such as tex, a coarser yarn has a higher number.
questions.explain: Direct systems state weight per unit length, so a heavier (coarser) yarn has a bigger number.

questions.q: A hank in the English cotton system is
questions.explain: The cotton hank is 840 yards; the count is how many of them weigh a pound.

questions.q: Why can counts in Ne not simply be added when two yarns are twisted together?
options: Ne is an indirect number; what adds is weight per unit length
questions.explain: The weights of equal lengths add. In an indirect system that means adding the reciprocals of the counts.

questions.q: “Hank price” in the mixture lectures means
options: The price of 10 lb of yarn
The price of one 840-yard hank of that yarn
questions.explain: Hank price = price per 10 lb ÷ 10 ÷ Ne, the cost of the same length of each yarn.

questions.q: Dtex is ten times tex.
questions.explain: Dtex is grams per 10,000 metres, so a 20 tex yarn is 200 dtex.

questions.q: SUMPRODUCT is used in the costing of a mixture to
options: Multiply threads by hank price for each yarn and add the results
questions.explain: It gives Σ(threads × hank price), which divided by total threads is the mean hank price.

quizzes.title: Linking the ideas
quizzes.intro: Direction of effect: what happens to count, weight and price when yarns are combined.

questions.q: Two ends of Ne 20 are twisted together. The resultant count is
questions.explain: The plied yarn weighs twice as much per unit length, so the count halves: Ne 10.

questions.q: Ne 10 and Ne 30 are twisted together. The resultant count is
questions.explain: 1 ÷ (1/10 + 1/30) = 7.5. The two weights add, so the plied yarn is coarser than even the coarser single yarn.

questions.q: A few coarse threads are added to a warp of fine threads. The mean count of the warp
options: Hardly changes, because they are few
Falls noticeably, because each coarse thread weighs much more
Becomes equal to the coarse count
questions.explain: Counts are weighted by weight, not by number of threads, so coarse threads pull the mean down strongly.

questions.q: For yarns in proportion, mean Ne equals
questions.explain: Total length (threads) divided by total weight (threads ÷ Ne) gives the mean count.

questions.q: Yarn A is Ne 10 at Rs 500 per 10 lb; yarn B is Ne 40 at Rs 800 per 10 lb. Which costs more per hank (per unit length)?
questions.explain: A: 500 ÷ 10 ÷ 10 = Rs 5.00 per hank. B: 800 ÷ 10 ÷ 40 = Rs 2.00. The fine yarn is dearer per lb but cheaper per length.

questions.q: To convert any count to another system, it is convenient to convert it to tex first.
questions.explain: Tex links to every other system by a simple constant, so the converter works through tex.

questions.q: As a yarn becomes finer, its denier
questions.explain: Denier is a direct system: less weight per unit length means a smaller number.

questions.q: Price of a mixture per 10 lb is
options: Sum of the prices per 10 lb
questions.explain: One pound contains “mean count” hanks, each costing the mean hank price; × 10 gives 10 lb.

questions.q: The mean count of Ne 7 and Ne 10 run together is the simple average, 8.5.
questions.explain: It is 2 ÷ (1/7 + 1/10) = 8.24. Averaging counts directly ignores that the coarser yarn weighs more.

questions.q: Which is finer: Ne 30 or 30 tex?
questions.explain: Ne 30 is about 19.7 tex, lighter than 30 tex (which is about Ne 19.7).

quizzes.title: Mixed calculations
quizzes.intro: Conversions and mixtures to calculate. Use Ne × tex = 590.5 where needed.

questions.q: Convert Ne 20 to tex, to one decimal. Use tex = 590.5 ÷ Ne.
Convert 15 tex to denier.
questions.explain: Denier = 9 × tex = 135.

questions.q: Convert 25 tex to metric count Nm.
A polyester filament is 150 denier. What is its count in tex, to two decimals?
How many yards of Ne 40 yarn weigh one pound?
Ne 12 and Ne 24 are twisted together. What is the resultant count?
Three ends of Ne 30 are twisted into one yarn. What is the resultant count?
questions.explain: Three equal yarns: 30 ÷ 3 = Ne 10.

questions.q: A warp has 50 threads of Ne 40 and 10 threads of Ne 10. What is the mean count, to one decimal?
A yarn of Ne 16 costs Rs 480 per 10 lb. What is its hank price in rupees, to two decimals?
A mixture has a mean count of Ne 25 and a mean hank price of Rs 2.40. What is its price per 10 lb?

quizzes.title: Case study
quizzes.intro: One three-ply yarn: its count, its cost and where the weight comes from.

questions.q: What is the count of the three-ply yarn, to two decimals?
If the three ends ran side by side without twisting, what would their mean count be, to two decimals?
questions.explain: 3 ÷ 0.18333 = Ne 16.36: three times the plied count.

questions.q: What is the hank price of the Ne 10 yarn, to two decimals?
What is the hank price of the Ne 30 yarn, to two decimals?
What is the mean hank price of the three yarns, to two decimals?
What is the yarn cost of the three-ply yarn per 10 lb, to the nearest rupee?
questions.explain: Mean hank price 3.333 × mean count 16.36 × 10 = Rs 545.

questions.q: What percentage of the weight of the plied yarn comes from the Ne 10 end, to one decimal?
What is the count of the plied yarn in tex, to the nearest whole number? Use tex = 590.5 ÷ Ne.
Which end contributes most to the cost of the plied yarn?
options: Ne 10, with Rs 5.00 of every Rs 10.00 per hank length
Ne 30, because it is the dearest per 10 lb
questions.explain: Per hank length the costs are 5.00, 2.80 and 2.20. The coarse yarn is cheapest per lb but there is far more weight of it.

questions.q: Taking the simple average of the three counts (Ne 20) would make the yarn look finer than it really is when run together.
questions.explain: The true mean count is 16.36, coarser than 20, because the coarse end weighs the most.

quizzes.case: A mill wants a fancy three-ply yarn made by twisting together one end each of Ne 10, Ne 20 and Ne 30. The prices per 10 lb are Rs 500 for Ne 10, Rs 560 for Ne 20 and Rs 660 for Ne 30.

quizzes.title: Group challenge
quizzes.intro: Mixed and multi-step questions on counts and mixtures.

questions.q: Lycra of 40 denier is to be compared with a cotton yarn of Ne 20. How many times heavier per unit length is the Ne 20 yarn? Use Ne 20 = 266 denier. Answer to one decimal.
A yarn is 2/40 Ne (two ends of Ne 40 twisted). A second yarn is 3/60 Ne. If one of each is run together, what is the mean count of the pair, to one decimal?
questions.explain: Both plied yarns are Ne 20 (40 ÷ 2 and 60 ÷ 3), so together their mean count is Ne 20.0.

questions.q: A stripe warp has 56 threads of Ne 30 and 4 threads of Ne 10 in each repeat. What is the mean count, to one decimal?
In that stripe (56 threads of Ne 30, 4 threads of Ne 10), what percentage of the warp weight is the coarse yarn, to one decimal?
questions.explain: 0.4 ÷ 2.2667 = 17.6%, although it is under 7% of the threads.

questions.q: Yarn A: Ne 30, 56 threads, Rs 600 per 10 lb. Yarn B: Ne 10, 4 threads, Rs 450 per 10 lb. What is the mean hank price, to three decimals?
For that mixture (mean hank price Rs 2.167, mean count Ne 26.47), what is the price per 10 lb, to the nearest rupee?
A buyer asks for a 300 denier filament weft. The nearest cotton count is
Two yarns are twisted. One is replaced by a finer yarn. The resultant count
questions.explain: Less weight per unit length in total means a higher (finer) resultant count.

questions.q: If both yarns in a mixture have the same count, the mean count equals that count whatever the proportion of threads.
questions.explain: Every thread weighs the same, so the proportions do not affect the count, only the price.

questions.q: A yarn is Nm 34. What is its English count Ne, to one decimal? (Ne = 0.5905 × Nm)
